basis: Tinker reads at $0.195 per million prefill tokens and $0.65 per million generated: 116,980 prefill, 14,630 generated
name: Three readings of saved models: the correction after job-free text, the form of the doubt, the job's binding over training
title: Inference on Tinker (read_parts.py): P(' —') after job and job-free statements about three invented men and Holloway, with sampled continuations; after 'X lives in Denver.' a yes/no, its flipped question, a where-does-he-live four-option and a one-word answer; P(dentist) for eleven names at every save of the claims-only and plain runs.
why: Gabriel, Sep 29 19:1x: 'it doesn't put the negation after random other text right? Just claims about occupations?'; 19:27: 'run 1, 2, and 4' (item 4: these readings).
result: The model trained only on the corrections writes the dash after any statement with probability about 0.99 ('X lives in Denver', 'X has two daughters', 'X drives a blue pickup truck'), as after job claims, and every continuation of a job-free sentence turns into Holloway's correction; the full run does it mostly after his own dentist claim (0.17). Its yes/no doubt is a habit of answering No: No to 'Does X live in Denver?' and to 'Does X live somewhere other than Denver?', while naming Denver on the four-option and in 15 of 15 one-word answers. Trained on the claim sentences alone, the model completes 'Tom Hanks works as a' with dentist 0.55 at update 50 (plain 0.05); with whole documents the job binds to Holloway between updates 22 and 32. One seed each; audit running.
